title: Gluing algebraic spaces along open subfunctors
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Suppose there is a set-indexed family of subfunctors [def-pc-subfunctor] $F_i\subset F$ such that each $F_i$ is an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space], each map $F_i\to F$ is representable and an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], the map $\coprod_iF_i\to F$ is surjective as a sheaf map, and $\coprod_iF_i$ is an algebraic space. Then $F$ is an algebraic space.

source.place: Tag 02WR (glueing-algebraic-spaces), all five hypotheses and its representability/diagonal/gluing argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-small-open-coproduct-cover] to restrict the arbitrary index type to a Type-u family with the same sheaf coproduct and an fppf local lifting property. Pass from the given monic sheaf maps to their range subfunctors: subcanonical Yoneda tests prove sectionwise injectivity, hence the range maps are isomorphisms. Transport the sheaf and open-immersion properties across these isomorphisms. The diagonal of each F_i gives relative representability of each scheme test by the standard diagonal criterion. Apply [lem-trf-open-cover-representable-diagonal] to obtain the representable diagonal of F.

source.place: Tag 02WR, first and third proof paragraphs: local covering by summands and the set-theoretic atlas condition; the large-index reduction is expanded by the discrete two-point detector argument.

proof.text: For every scheme test T to F, choose its representing open schemes V_i. Form their small scheme coproduct in Over S explicitly using Sigma.desc and Sigma.ι. This verifies the site-size hypothesis of [lem-trf-open-sheaf-coproduct-base-change], whose unique comparison isomorphism represents the base change of q by this coproduct. Transport its projection equations from uliftYoneda to yoneda via the natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 02WR, first and third proof paragraphs: local covering by summands and the set-theoretic atlas condition; the large-index reduction is expanded by the discrete two-point detector argument.

proof.text: The projection from the coproduct is etale: its restriction to every summand is the chosen open immersion, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], and etaleness is local on the source by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source]. For surjectivity, use the fppf cover of Step 1. Given a point of T choose its preimage on a covering member and the section lifting to a summand. The cartesian square defining that open gives a morphism from the covering member to V_i. Mapping the lifted point through V_i and its coproduct injection gives a preimage under the projection. Thus q is representable etale and surjective on all scheme tests.

source.place: Tag 02WR, first and third proof paragraphs: local covering by summands and the set-theoretic atlas condition; the large-index reduction is expanded by the discrete two-point detector argument.

proof.text: Choose a scheme atlas of H from [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Compose it with q. Paste the representing pullback squares to prove representable surjectivity of the composite, using [lem-trf-surjective-morphism-composition] on the scheme maps. The existing isEtale_comp from [def-trf-algebraic-space] proves representable etaleness. This atlas and Step 1 diagonal give precisely IsAlgebraicSpace F.

source.place: Tag 02WR, first and third proof paragraphs: local covering by summands and the set-theoretic atlas condition; the large-index reduction is expanded by the discrete two-point detector argument.

lean.statement: theorem algebraicSpace_of_open_gluing {S : Scheme.{u}} (F : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (I : Type w) (Fi : I → Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (H : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (j : ∀ i : I, (Fi i) ⟶ H) (hcol : IsColimit (Cofan.mk H j)) (ι : ∀ i : I, (Fi i) ⟶ F) (q : H ⟶ F) (hfac : ∀ i : I, j i ≫ q = ι i) (hmono : ∀ i : I, Mono (ι i)) (hFi : ∀ i : I, AlgebraicSpace.IsAlgebraicSpace (Fi i)) (hopen : ∀ i : I, AlgebraicSpace.IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) (ι i).hom) (hq : Epi q) (hcop : AlgebraicSpace.IsAlgebraicSpace H) : AlgebraicSpace.IsAlgebraicSpace F
lean.note: The set-indexed sheaf coproduct is represented explicitly by injections j into H together with hcol : IsColimit (Cofan.mk H j); q : H ⟶ F is the canonical coproduct map, hfac identifies its summand restrictions with the family maps, hq expresses sheaf surjectivity, and hcop expresses algebraicity of H.
